coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P11
names: P11 -- landscaped median strip connecting Mission Bay Circle to P11A
record.summary: A tree-lined median strip running within the road right-of-way, connecting the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout east to the P11A half-circle island; a real, already-landscaped median per satellite imagery, hand-traced with the property owner's guidance and fit to a rotated rectangle. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P11/11A' together among the parcels already managed by SF Recreation and Parks (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- owner-guided satellite trace, idealized to a fitted rectangle rather than left as a raw hand-traced outline. Not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. street_clip_exempt=true: this is a real median strip that sits entirely within the paved road right-of-way by design -- clipping it against the generic street buffer would zero it out entirely, not correct a mispositioning. Owner-approved exception.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery, guided directly by the owner's own marked-up screenshot (their drawn outline extracted from the photo via ORB feature-matching/homography), then fit to an idealized road-aligned rectangle per the owner's description of the real shape.

milestones.text: Already part of RPD's managed open-space inventory as 'P11/11A' (not listed among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), per OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation to the Mission Bay CAC -- an upper bound on when this median was built, not its actual construction date

open_questions: No public source names this specific median strip or gives its own construction date; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already RPD-managed by that date (grouped with P11A), which is an upper bound, not a build date.

A separate, later OCII source (the Nov 2024 CAC deck, src-ocii-openspace-2024) instead groups the label 'P11' together with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 under the still-interim 'Mission Bay Commons' area near 3rd Street and Mission Bay Boulevard -- a different location from this record's median strip near Mission Bay Circle. This repo's own digitization_method log already describes correcting an earlier session's own wrong location guess for P11 (made from that same source note) after the property owner pointed to this median strip instead; the underlying conflict between the two OCII documents' own use of 'P11' is not resolved here, only flagged.
Owner/operator beyond 'part of RPD's Mission Bay open-space inventory' not confirmed by any source found.
